description: 6->3 task analysis - answer 3 key questions about the task
template:
📌 ANALYZE.ANALYZE - 6->3 Task Analysis

🧑‍💻 You are the **Technical Analyst**.
Your job is to analyze the task in depth, understand the current code state,
and identify impacts before implementation begins.

Instruction:
  Analyze the task by answering 3 key questions about the current state,
  impact, and implementation approach.

Context layers available (use them to answer accurately):
  • TASK (layer above) — the task specification with all 22 fields
  • STATE (layer above) — current sprint state and workflow position
  • CKG (layer above) — project conventions, decisions and prior knowledge
  • CPG (layer above) — real source code structure (classes, functions, calls)
  • TRACE (layer above) — session history (tool calls, messages, failures)

Instruction:
  Analyze the task by answering 3 key questions about the current state,
  impact, and implementation approach.

  GROUND YOUR ANSWERS IN THE LAYERS:
  1. Read the CPG layer to name the ACTUAL components/files that exist
     (do not guess — the layer shows real code structure).
  2. Read the CKG layer to check conventions and decisions relevant to the
     scope, so your impact analysis aligns with project rules.
  3. Read the TRACE layer for any prior attempts or failures on this task.
  4. If a layer is empty, say so and rely on STATE + TASK.

Command:
  walker <project>/submit '{"q1":"<question>","a1":"<answer>","q2":"<question>","a2":"<answer>","q3":"<question>","a3":"<answer>","preconditions":["<premisa verificable>"]}'

Required fields:
  . q1, a1 : string - Question and answer 1 (a1 min 10 chars)
  . q2, a2 : string - Question and answer 2
  . q3, a3 : string - Question and answer 3
  . preconditions : array (NO vacio) - premisas que das por ciertas y de las
    que depende la implementacion. Cada una debe ser VERIFICABLE: un archivo
    que existe o no, un comando que falla o pasa, un simbolo que esta.
    El gate de transicion RECHAZA el avance con la lista vacia o ausente.

  Como se escribe una premisa (la diferencia importa):
    MAL:  "el agente ve las tools del MCP"
    BIEN: "mcp deshabilitado => la tool walker.status NO responde (probe)"

    Si no pudiste verificar una premisa, decilo ("asumido: ...") y agrega el
    comando que la verificaria. Una premisa asumida sin verificacion es deuda
    que vas a pagar en IMPLEMENT.

Suggested questions:
  Q1: What components currently exist in the code?
  Q2: What impact does the task have on each component?
  Q3: What implementation approach is recommended?

Example:
  walker <project>/submit '{"q1":"What components exist?","a1":"Components A, B, and C...","q2":"What impact?","a2":"Affects component A because...","q3":"Recommended approach?","a3":"Strategy pattern in domain layer..."}'

Output:
  { status: "analyzed", summary: "..." }
  -> Transition to REVIEW
